results.title: Acme Robotics | About
results.content: Acme Robotics builds autonomous mobile robots for warehouse picking. Founded in 2015 in Boston by Dana Whitfield and Raj Menon, the company ships the Picker One robot to grocery and apparel distribution centers across North America and employs about 640 people.

results.title: Acme Robotics profile - Logistics Weekly
results.content: Acme's fleet software coordinates mixed fleets of robots and human pickers. The company says customers see 2-3x picks per labor hour. Its main market is mid-size regional grocers that cannot afford fully automated warehouses.

results.title: Picker One launches second generation
results.content: The second-generation Picker One adds a suction gripper and a 30% longer battery. Acme said 41 sites now run the robot, up from 18 a year earlier.

message.content: Acme Robotics is a Boston-based manufacturer of autonomous mobile robots for warehouse picking, founded in 2015 by Dana Whitfield and Raj Menon. Its Picker One robot, now in its second generation, runs at 41 distribution centers, mostly mid-size regional grocers, where Acme reports 2-3x more picks per labor hour. The company employs about 640 people. In March 2025 it raised a $120 million Series C led by Northbridge Ventures, bringing total funding to $210 million, and it intends to expand into Europe in 2026. Sources: acmerobotics.example, logisticsweekly.example, venturewire.example.
